bull_bear.body:
- Brand heritage: founded in 1893, with over 130 years of heritage and consumer confidence behind the Amrutanjan pain-relief franchise
- Category leadership positions: Amrutanjan Roll On is stated to be the leader in its category, and Comfy occupies the 4th position nationally in the mass pad segment
- Distribution scale: 3,994 distributors and sub-distributors and 1.13 Mn rubefacient outlets, with 44,000 new chemist outlets added during FY2026
- Category outperformance: AHCL outperformed the Rubefacients category and other major players on volume growth, and its Body Ache volume growth was significantly ahead of the category across all quarters of FY26
- Owned manufacturing base of five state-of-the-art units, with the new greenfield sanitary napkin plant giving design and supply-chain control over the Comfy brand
- R&D and quality systems: a Quality by Design approach, clinical studies validating flagship products, and a Quality Management System spanning R&D, procurement, manufacturing, packaging and delivery
- Digitisation depth: 70% of critical processes automated, SAP enterprise processes across manufacturing, supply chain and finance, Sales Force Automation for Modern Trade, and a Distributor Management System covering more than 387 distributors
- Concept retail presence through World of Amrutanjan experience stores in Delhi, Ahmedabad and Chennai
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material and packaging cost volatility — The MD&A Risk and Concern section names unpredictable fluctuation in key raw material prices among the long-term risks to the business, and the Opportunities and Threats section flags increase in packaging material costs as directly impacting profit margins. Management separately anticipated COGS inflation in FY2026 on account of the Middle East conflict affecting crude prices and global supply chains, mitigated only partially through calibrated pricing.
- Regulatory change affecting product categories and business plans — Major changes in government policies and regulations are listed among the long-term business risks, and changes in regulatory compliances are named as a threat impacting the Company's business plans. The Chairman states the electrolyte drink category experienced severe regulatory hurdles for the past 3 years, which has been a setback to growth, illustrating that regulatory risk in this business is realised rather than theoretical.
- Category and revenue concentration in pain management — The majority of the Company's revenue (62%) is derived from the Head and Body categories, which management reaffirms as the primary revenue contributors for future growth. This makes the earnings base structurally dependent on the rubefacients franchise and on the continued outperformance of a single brand family.
- Weak penetration in P3 markets alongside strong competition — The Opportunities and Threats section names low penetration of AHCL products in P3 markets and strong competition as challenging the Company's market penetration. Distribution strength is concentrated in South and East India, which the Chairman identifies as the traditional strong markets the Company is trying to expand beyond, so growth depends on executing in geographies where the brand is weakest.
- New product launches failing to gain traction — The MD&A explicitly lists the risk of new product launches not panning out among the long-term risks. This matters because the stated growth strategy leans heavily on innovation, with a launch pipeline including Period Panties, Panty liners, women's razors, Plastry bandages and the relaunched Jiffy brand, and on the loss-making Women's Hygiene and Beverages segments turning around.
- Supply chain disruption — Supply chain disruptions are named among the long-term risks associated with the business, and the MD&A notes that global macroeconomic uncertainties and geopolitical developments continue to influence commodity prices, freight and supply-chain costs. R&D mitigation includes collaborating with alternate suppliers to mitigate single vendor risk, which implies vendor concentration exists in parts of the input base.
- Information and cyber security — The BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table identifies Information Security / Cyber Security as a risk, citing non-availability of service or failure of multiple systems leading to business disruption due to lack of adequate process, cyber security, and disaster recovery systems. The dependency is material because SAP underpins manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and financial accounting, and sales run through Sales Force Automation and a Distributor Management System.
- Product liability and customer welfare — The BRSR material issues table identifies Customer Welfare as a risk, noting that compromised customer welfare will lead to lawsuits and product recalls resulting in reputation damage, and that adhering to high quality ingredients and manufacturing standards leads to market competition and cost pressures. For an OTC healthcare brand whose principal asset is over a century of consumer trust, a quality failure is a direct threat to the moat.
- Employee health and safety, and high employee attrition — The BRSR material issues table identifies Employee Health and Safety as a risk from non-adoption of adequate safety practices leading to accidents and injuries, mitigated through site-based safety committees, permits to work and incident reporting. Separately, the BRSR turnover-rate table discloses permanent-employee attrition of 31.55% in FY2025-26 against 32.00% in FY2024-25, a structurally high level for a business whose distribution expansion depends on field sales execution.

business.body: AHCL manufactures and markets ayurvedic pharmaceutical preparations, fruit-based beverages and women's hygiene products, selling to consumers through retail, stockist and distributor networks as well as modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels. Its OTC portfolio covers headache and body-ache rubefacients, congestion relief and wound care under the Amrutanjan and Relief brands, while Comfy addresses period care and women's personal care. The Company also runs an electrolyte and rehydration beverage business and has established a cGMP-certified Allopathic division producing OTC monograph topical products for export to the US and other regulated markets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **OTC / Pain Management:** Amrutanjan Yellow Balm, Amrutanjan White Balm, Amrutanjan Head Roll-On, Back Pain Roll-On, Maha Strong, Ortho Oil, Jiffy (spray and oral analgesic formats), Amrutanjan Plastry bandages
- **OTC / Congestion Relief:** Relief Inhaler, Relief Rubs
- **Women's Hygiene & Personal Care:** Comfy sanitary napkins, Comfy XL, Comfy Night pads, Comfy Silky Smoothe women's razors, Close and Clean women's razors
- **Beverages:** Amrutanjan Electro+ ORS, Amrutanjan Enerlyte

outlook.body:
- Four core pillars guiding growth: strengthening the power brands Amrutanjan and Comfy, distribution expansion, product innovation, and operational excellence via digitisation
- Widen distribution beyond the traditional strongholds in South and East India while deepening penetration in existing strong markets, targeting 1,00,000 direct chemist outlets by FY2027
- Evolve the Amrutanjan brand beyond its heritage in headache relief into a trusted partner in comprehensive pain management, addressing body pain, muscle pain and joint care
- Build Comfy from a period-care brand into a broader women's hygiene and wellness brand, extending into Night pads, Period Panties, Panty liners and women's hair removal
- Expand participation across e-commerce and quick commerce, and build the D2C channel, backed by investment in digital marketing and e-commerce human capital
- Build a global consumer healthcare business, with the US market entered via Amazon US and a new cGMP-certified Allopathic division producing OTC monograph topical products for regulated markets
- Expand manufacturing capacity and secure design and supply-chain control over Comfy through the greenfield Telangana sanitary napkin plant
- Advance digitisation as a strategic pillar, moving from 70% of critical processes automated towards close to 100%, supported by SAP, Sales Force Automation and the Distributor Management System
- Address rural markets through rural van activity, low-unit-price packs and expansion of the distributor and sub-distributor network
- Continue investing in brand-building through mass media, digital channels, sampling and merchandising
- Build the electrolyte and rehydration category over the long term through consumer education, expansion of distribution touch points and product innovation, despite the regulatory hurdles of the past three years
- Expand investment in human capital across learning and growth, sales and marketing, IT and supply chain
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The dominant expansion project of FY2026 is the greenfield sanitary napkin manufacturing facility at Seetharampur Village, Shabad Mandal, Rangareddy District, Telangana, approximately 45 km from Hyderabad. Described in the Corporate Overview as a I150 crore investment, it is AHCL's fifth manufacturing plant, spread across 10 acres with a 1.40 lakh sq. ft. built-up area and equipped with two fully automated high-speed production lines imported from Japan, which the Company describes as making it one of India's fastest sanitary napkin manufacturing facilities. Planned annual production capacity is 700 million sanitary napkins, and the site is expected to generate 200 direct and 150 indirect employment opportunities. The Corporate Overview states the facility has been commissioned, while the Chairman's message states the plant will be commissioned in the first quarter of 2027; management says it will give design and supply-chain control over the Comfy brand and enable further growth in market share. Sustainability features designed into the plant include rainwater harvesting, an on-site Sewage Treatment Plant, waste recycling systems and energy-efficient LED lighting, with solar power planned for the future. Separately, to expand its global presence the Company has established a new Allopathic division supported by a cGMP-certified manufacturing facility, recently commissioned and equipped with advanced manufacturing and testing equipment, dedicated to OTC monograph topical application products registered with the USFDA and exported to the USA and other regulated markets. Existing OTC manufacturing is at Alathur (Kancheepuram District, Tamil Nadu) and Uppal (Hyderabad, Telangana), with the beverage plant at Aranvoyal Village (Tiruvallur District, Tamil Nadu); of the OTC units the Company says only that "With a capacity of 1,800 MT, we are well-equipped to meet market demand", without stating the date the figure is measured at. Non-manufacturing footprint expansion includes the addition of 44,000 new chemist outlets during FY2026 with plans to add 1,00,000 chemists by FY2027, expansion of the Distributor Management System from more than 387 distributors to a planned 400 in FY2027, and World of Amrutanjan experience stores in Delhi, Ahmedabad and Chennai. The Vision and Outlook spread lists Capacity Expansion, Digital Transformation and Demand Outlook and Brand Strategy as headings, but the bundle truncates mid-sentence after the Cost Environment paragraph, so the body text under those three headings is not available in either the capex_expansion or strategy_outlook bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural shift towards self-care and preventive healthcare: the Indian consumer is increasingly embracing self-care and taking greater responsibility for managing everyday health needs, which management describes as creating a compelling long-term opportunity for the OTC healthcare industry
- The Indian Health and Wellness market is valued at $15B (source IQVIA) with the OTC segment, at 60%, the largest contributor
- The Rubefacients category grew on both value and volume in FY26 in a consumption-led expansion, with AHCL outperforming the category and other major players on volume growth
- The majority of the Company's revenue (62%) is derived from the Head and Body categories, which management reaffirms as the primary revenue contributors for future growth
- Quick commerce has emerged as a particularly important channel for consumer healthcare products, especially in urban markets where immediacy of need significantly influences purchase decisions
- Improving rural demand supported by better agricultural output, favourable monsoon conditions, government welfare programmes and higher rural income levels, with rural markets gradually narrowing the growth gap with urban markets
- Premiumisation across FMCG categories as consumers seek superior quality, convenience, health benefits and enhanced experience
- COGS inflation anticipated in FY2026 on account of the ongoing Middle East conflict impacting crude prices and global supply chains, partially mitigated through calibrated pricing actions
- Global macroeconomic uncertainties continue to influence commodity prices, freight and supply-chain costs, against which the Company is focused on improving sourcing, manufacturing and supply-chain efficiencies, accelerating digitisation and maintaining disciplined cost management
- Regulatory change, input-cost volatility and competitive intensity require disciplined execution, while trusted brands, expanding distribution and innovation provide the foundation for long-term value creation
- Growth opportunities identified for the upcoming year: building distinctiveness in existing brands, launching new products across existing and new categories, expanding existing brands into weaker markets, scaling distribution and the D2C channel, and driving modern trade and e-commerce
- Export business momentum, with Africa contributing 81% of export revenue in FY26 and revenues from other international markets doubling year on year, supporting geographical diversification

currentContext.expansion: The dominant expansion project of FY2026 is the greenfield sanitary napkin manufacturing facility at Seetharampur Village, Shabad Mandal, Rangareddy District, Telangana, approximately 45 km from Hyderabad. Described in the Corporate Overview as a I150 crore investment, it is AHCL's fifth manufacturing plant, spread across 10 acres with a 1.40 lakh sq. ft. built-up area and equipped with two fully automated high-speed production lines imported from Japan, which the Company describes as making it one of India's fastest sanitary napkin manufacturing facilities. Planned annual production capacity is 700 million sanitary napkins, and the site is expected to generate 200 direct and 150 indirect employment opportunities. The Corporate Overview states the facility has been commissioned, while the Chairman's message states the plant will be commissioned in the first quarter of 2027; management says it will give design and supply-chain control over the Comfy brand and enable further growth in market share. Sustainability features designed into the plant include rainwater harvesting, an on-site Sewage Treatment Plant, waste recycling systems and energy-efficient LED lighting, with solar power planned for the future. Separately, to expand its global presence the Company has established a new Allopathic division supported by a cGMP-certified manufacturing facility, recently commissioned and equipped with advanced manufacturing and testing equipment, dedicated to OTC monograph topical application products registered with the USFDA and exported to the USA and other regulated markets. Existing OTC manufacturing is at Alathur (Kancheepuram District, Tamil Nadu) and Uppal (Hyderabad, Telangana), with the beverage plant at Aranvoyal Village (Tiruvallur District, Tamil Nadu); of the OTC units the Company says only that "With a capacity of 1,800 MT, we are well-equipped to meet market demand", without stating the date the figure is measured at. Non-manufacturing footprint expansion includes the addition of 44,000 new chemist outlets during FY2026 with plans to add 1,00,000 chemists by FY2027, expansion of the Distributor Management System from more than 387 distributors to a planned 400 in FY2027, and World of Amrutanjan experience stores in Delhi, Ahmedabad and Chennai. The Vision and Outlook spread lists Capacity Expansion, Digital Transformation and Demand Outlook and Brand Strategy as headings, but the bundle truncates mid-sentence after the Cost Environment paragraph, so the body text under those three headings is not available in either the capex_expansion or strategy_outlook bundle.

risks.risk: Raw material and packaging cost volatility
risks.note: The MD&A Risk and Concern section names unpredictable fluctuation in key raw material prices among the long-term risks to the business, and the Opportunities and Threats section flags increase in packaging material costs as directly impacting profit margins. Management separately anticipated COGS inflation in FY2026 on account of the Middle East conflict affecting crude prices and global supply chains, mitigated only partially through calibrated pricing.

risks.risk: Regulatory change affecting product categories and business plans
risks.note: Major changes in government policies and regulations are listed among the long-term business risks, and changes in regulatory compliances are named as a threat impacting the Company's business plans. The Chairman states the electrolyte drink category experienced severe regulatory hurdles for the past 3 years, which has been a setback to growth, illustrating that regulatory risk in this business is realised rather than theoretical.

risks.risk: Category and revenue concentration in pain management
risks.note: The majority of the Company's revenue (62%) is derived from the Head and Body categories, which management reaffirms as the primary revenue contributors for future growth. This makes the earnings base structurally dependent on the rubefacients franchise and on the continued outperformance of a single brand family.

risks.risk: Weak penetration in P3 markets alongside strong competition
risks.note: The Opportunities and Threats section names low penetration of AHCL products in P3 markets and strong competition as challenging the Company's market penetration. Distribution strength is concentrated in South and East India, which the Chairman identifies as the traditional strong markets the Company is trying to expand beyond, so growth depends on executing in geographies where the brand is weakest.

risks.risk: New product launches failing to gain traction
risks.note: The MD&A explicitly lists the risk of new product launches not panning out among the long-term risks. This matters because the stated growth strategy leans heavily on innovation, with a launch pipeline including Period Panties, Panty liners, women's razors, Plastry bandages and the relaunched Jiffy brand, and on the loss-making Women's Hygiene and Beverages segments turning around.

Supply chain disruptions are named among the long-term risks associated with the business, and the MD&A notes that global macroeconomic uncertainties and geopolitical developments continue to influence commodity prices, freight and supply-chain costs. R&D mitigation includes collaborating with alternate suppliers to mitigate single vendor risk, which implies vendor concentration exists in parts of the input base.

The BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table identifies Information Security / Cyber Security as a risk, citing non-availability of service or failure of multiple systems leading to business disruption due to lack of adequate process, cyber security, and disaster recovery systems. The dependency is material because SAP underpins manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and financial accounting, and sales run through Sales Force Automation and a Distributor Management System.

The BRSR material issues table identifies Customer Welfare as a risk, noting that compromised customer welfare will lead to lawsuits and product recalls resulting in reputation damage, and that adhering to high quality ingredients and manufacturing standards leads to market competition and cost pressures. For an OTC healthcare brand whose principal asset is over a century of consumer trust, a quality failure is a direct threat to the moat.

risks.risk: Employee health and safety, and high employee attrition
risks.note: The BRSR material issues table identifies Employee Health and Safety as a risk from non-adoption of adequate safety practices leading to accidents and injuries, mitigated through site-based safety committees, permits to work and incident reporting. Separately, the BRSR turnover-rate table discloses permanent-employee attrition of 31.55% in FY2025-26 against 32.00% in FY2024-25, a structurally high level for a business whose distribution expansion depends on field sales execution.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Amrutanjan Health Care Limited is a Chennai-headquartered over-the-counter healthcare and consumer goods company, founded in 1893, whose Amrutanjan pain-relief and Comfy women's hygiene brands anchor a portfolio spanning pain management, congestion relief, beverages and feminine hygiene.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: AHCL manufactures and markets ayurvedic pharmaceutical preparations, fruit-based beverages and women's hygiene products, selling to consumers through retail, stockist and distributor networks as well as modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels. Its OTC portfolio covers headache and body-ache rubefacients, congestion relief and wound care under the Amrutanjan and Relief brands, while Comfy addresses period care and women's personal care. The Company also runs an electrolyte and rehydration beverage business and has established a cGMP-certified Allopathic division producing OTC monograph topical products for export to the US and other regulated markets.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **OTC / Pain Management:** Amrutanjan Yellow Balm, Amrutanjan White Balm, Amrutanjan Head Roll-On, Back Pain Roll-On, Maha Strong, Ortho Oil, Jiffy (spray and oral analgesic formats), Amrutanjan Plastry bandages
- **OTC / Congestion Relief:** Relief Inhaler, Relief Rubs
- **Women's Hygiene & Personal Care:** Comfy sanitary napkins, Comfy XL, Comfy Night pads, Comfy Silky Smoothe women's razors, Close and Clean women's razors
- **Beverages:** Amrutanjan Electro+ ORS, Amrutanjan Enerlyte

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian retail consumers reached through retail, stockist and distributor networks and the modern trade channel
- E-commerce and quick-commerce platforms in India
- Rural and semi-urban India via distributor and sub-distributor networks
- Chemist and general trade outlets, with traditional strongholds in South and East India
- 28 Indian states served domestically
- 19 international countries, with Africa the largest export destination at 81% of total exports in FY26
- United States OTC healthcare market, entered in FY2025-26 through Amazon US

certifications.body:

- ISO 22000 Food Safety Management System (beverage plant)
- Good Manufacturing Practices under the Indian Drugs and Cosmetics Act
- cGMP-certified Allopathic manufacturing facility
- USFDA OTC Monograph registration for products exported to the …

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift towards self-care and preventive healthcare: the Indian consumer is increasingly embracing self-care and taking greater responsibility for managing everyday health needs, which management describes as creating a compelling long-term opportunity for the OTC healthcare industry
- The Indian Health and Wellness market is valued at $15B (source IQVIA) with the OTC segment, at 60%, the largest contributor
- The Rubefacients category grew on both value and volume in FY26 in a consumption-led expansion, with AHCL outperforming the category and other major players on volume growth
- The majority of the Company's revenue (62%) is derived from the Head and Body categories, which management reaffirms as the primary revenue contributors for future growth
- Quick commerce has emerged as a particularly important channel for consumer healthcare products, especially in urban markets where immediacy of need significantly influences purchase decisions
- Improving rural demand supported by better agricultural output, favourable monsoon conditions, government welfare programmes and higher rural income levels, with rural markets gradually narrowing the growth gap with urban markets
- Premiumisation across FMCG categories as consumers seek superior quality, convenience, health benefits and enhanced experience
- COGS inflation anticipated in FY2026 on account of the ongoing Middle East conflict impacting crude prices and global supply chains, partially mitigated through calibrated pricing actions
- Global macroeconomic uncertainties continue to influence commodity prices, freight and supply-chain costs, against which the Company is focused on improving sourcing, manufacturing and supply-chain efficiencies, accelerating digitisation and maintaining disciplined cost management
- Regulatory change, input-cost volatility and competitive intensity require disciplined execution, while trusted brands, expanding distribution and innovation provide the foundation for long-term value creation
- Growth opportunities identified for the upcoming year: building distinctiveness in existing brands, launching new products across existing and new categories, expanding existing brands into weaker markets, scaling distribution and the D2C channel, and driving modern trade and e-commerce
- Export business momentum, with Africa contributing 81% of export revenue in FY26 and revenues from other international markets doubling year on year, supporting geographical diversification

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Four core pillars guiding growth: strengthening the power brands Amrutanjan and Comfy, distribution expansion, product innovation, and operational excellence via digitisation
- Widen distribution beyond the traditional strongholds in South and East India while deepening penetration in existing strong markets, targeting 1,00,000 direct chemist outlets by FY2027
- Evolve the Amrutanjan brand beyond its heritage in headache relief into a trusted partner in comprehensive pain management, addressing body pain, muscle pain and joint care
- Build Comfy from a period-care brand into a broader women's hygiene and wellness brand, extending into Night pads, Period Panties, Panty liners and women's hair removal
- Expand participation across e-commerce and quick commerce, and build the D2C channel, backed by investment in digital marketing and e-commerce human capital
- Build a global consumer healthcare business, with the US market entered via Amazon US and a new cGMP-certified Allopathic division producing OTC monograph topical products for regulated markets
- Expand manufacturing capacity and secure design and supply-chain control over Comfy through the greenfield Telangana sanitary napkin plant
- Advance digitisation as a strategic pillar, moving from 70% of critical processes automated towards close to 100%, supported by SAP, Sales Force Automation and the Distributor Management System
- Address rural markets through rural van activity, low-unit-price packs and expansion of the distributor and sub-distributor network
- Continue investing in brand-building through mass media, digital channels, sampling and merchandising
- Build the electrolyte and rehydration category over the long term through consumer education, expansion of distribution touch points and product innovation, despite the regulatory hurdles of the past three years
- Expand investment in human capital across learning and growth, sales and marketing, IT and supply chain
